name: Adam
bio: Adam was the first man, formed by God from the dust of the ground and given the breath of life. God placed him in the garden of Eden to tend it and gave him Eve as his wife. Through his disobedience sin and death entered the world, yet God promised a coming Redeemer. The New Testament presents Christ as the 'last Adam' who brings life where the first Adam brought death.
tl: God forms Adam from the dust
Placed in Eden to tend the garden
God makes Eve and brings her to Adam
les: Adam tried to hide from God after he sinned. What helps you come to God honestly instead of hiding?
Where Adam failed, Jesus obeyed. How does knowing Christ as the 'last Adam' give you hope today?

name: Eve
bio: Eve was the first woman, made by God from Adam's side to be a helper suitable for him. Deceived by the serpent, she ate the forbidden fruit and gave it to Adam. Even in judgment God gave a promise that her seed would crush the serpent's head. Adam named her Eve because she was the mother of all living.
tl: God makes the woman from Adam's rib
Eats the fruit and gives to Adam
Named Eve, mother of all living
les: The serpent began by questioning what God said. How can you hold on to God's Word when doubts come?
God spoke a promise of rescue right after the fall. Where have you seen God's mercy meet you after a failure?

name: Noah
bio: Noah was a righteous man who walked with God in a corrupt generation. God told him to build an ark to save his family and the animals from the flood. He obeyed in faith, and after the waters receded he built an altar and worshipped. God made a covenant with him, sealed by the rainbow, never again to destroy the earth by flood.
tl: Finds grace in the eyes of the LORD
God commands him to build the ark
Enters the ark as the flood begins
Builds an altar after the flood
les: Noah obeyed for years before he saw a single raindrop. What is God asking you to keep doing faithfully, even when results are slow?
The rainbow is a sign of God's faithfulness. What reminders of His promises can you keep in front of you?

name: Abraham
bio: Abraham, first called Abram, was called by God to leave his homeland for a land God would show him. God promised to make him a great nation and to bless all families of the earth through him. He believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness. His faith was tested when God asked him to offer Isaac, and God provided a ram in his place.
tl: God calls Abram to leave his country
Abram departs as the LORD spoke
Dies in a good old age
les: Abraham went out not knowing where he was going. What step of trust might God be asking of you?
'God will provide himself a lamb.' How does Abraham's story point you to Jesus, the Lamb God provided?

name: Sarah
meaning: lady; princess; princess of the multitude
bio: Sarah, first called Sarai, was Abraham's wife and travelled with him in faith. She was barren for many years and once laughed at God's promise of a son in her old age. God kept His word, and she bore Isaac at ninety. Scripture honors her as a woman who judged Him faithful who had promised.
tl: Is any thing too hard for the LORD?
God hath made me to laugh
les: Sarah tried to make God's promise happen her own way with Hagar. Where are you tempted to rush God's timing?
Her laugh of doubt became a laugh of joy. What would it look like to trust that nothing is too hard for the Lord?

name: Isaac
bio: Isaac was the son of promise, born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age. As a young man he was laid on the altar on Mount Moriah before God provided a ram. He married Rebekah and became the father of Esau and Jacob. Isaac was a peaceable man who reopened his father's wells and received God's covenant promises.
tl: Meditating in the field when Rebekah comes
God renews the covenant with him
les: Isaac trusted his father on the way up the mountain. How does trusting your heavenly Father shape hard seasons?
Isaac prayed for his wife when she could not conceive. Who can you bring to the Lord in prayer this week?

name: Rebekah
bio: Rebekah was the wife of Isaac, chosen when she generously offered water to Abraham's servant and his camels. She willingly left her family to go and marry Isaac. She bore twins, Esau and Jacob, and God told her the elder would serve the younger. Later she arranged for Jacob to deceive Isaac, which led to painful separation from her favorite son.
tl: Offers water to the servant's camels
The elder shall serve the younger
les: Rebekah's kindness to a stranger opened the door to God's plan. How can small acts of generosity be part of His work through you?
She had God's promise but chose deception to secure it. How can you trust God to keep His word without manipulating outcomes?

name: Jacob
bio: Jacob was the younger twin of Esau who obtained his brother's birthright and blessing by cunning. Fleeing from Esau, he met God at Bethel in a dream of a ladder to heaven. After years with Laban he returned home, wrestled with God, and was renamed Israel. His twelve sons became the fathers of the twelve tribes.
tl: Dreams of the ladder at Bethel
les: God met Jacob while he was running from his own mistakes. How has God pursued you in your weakest moments?
Jacob would not let go until he was blessed. What do you need to bring to God with that kind of persistence?

name: Rachel
bio: Rachel was the beloved wife of Jacob, for whom he served Laban fourteen years. For years she was barren and envied her sister Leah. God remembered her and she bore Joseph, and later Benjamin, dying in childbirth near Bethlehem. Jeremiah pictures her weeping for her children, a passage Matthew links to the birth of Jesus.
tl: Buried on the way to Bethlehem
les: Rachel's longing turned into envy. How can you bring unmet desires to God without comparing yourself to others?
'God remembered Rachel.' What does it mean to you that God remembers you?

name: Joseph
bio: Joseph was Jacob's favored son, who dreamed that his family would bow to him. His jealous brothers sold him into slavery in Egypt, and he was later falsely accused and imprisoned. God gave him wisdom to interpret Pharaoh's dreams, and he rose to rule Egypt and save many from famine. He forgave his brothers, seeing God's good purpose in all that happened.
tl: Given a coat of many colours
The LORD is with him in prison
Ye thought evil, God meant it for good
les: Joseph stayed faithful in slavery and in prison. Where do you need to trust that the Lord is with you even now?
Joseph forgave those who hurt him deeply. Is there someone God is inviting you to release into His hands?

name: Moses
bio: Moses was born a Hebrew in Egypt, hidden in an ark of bulrushes, and raised in Pharaoh's household. After fleeing to Midian, he met God at the burning bush and was sent to deliver Israel. Through him God brought the plagues, parted the Red Sea, and gave the Law at Sinai. He led Israel through the wilderness for forty years and saw the promised land before he died.
tl: Placed in an ark of bulrushes
God reveals I AM THAT I AM
Stretches his hand over the sea
Dies in the land of Moab
les: Moses felt unqualified, yet God said, 'Certainly I will be with thee.' Where do you need God's presence more than your own ability?
Moses was called the meekest man on earth. What does humble leadership look like in your home or work?

name: Miriam
bio: Miriam was the sister of Moses and Aaron. As a girl she watched over baby Moses in the Nile and arranged for his own mother to nurse him. After the Red Sea crossing she led the women of Israel in song as a prophetess. When she spoke against Moses she was struck with leprosy, and was healed after Moses prayed for her.
tl: Leads the women with a timbrel
Sings, Sing ye to the LORD
les: Miriam led God's people in worship after deliverance. How can you lead others in praise for what God has done?
Her jealousy brought discipline, yet Moses prayed for her healing. How can you respond with grace when others wrong you?

name: Aaron
meaning: a teacher; lofty; mountain of strength
bio: Aaron was the elder brother of Moses and spoke for him before Pharaoh. God appointed him as Israel's first high priest. While Moses was on the mount, Aaron gave in to the people and made the golden calf. God still used him; his rod budded to confirm his priesthood, and his line served as priests.
tl: God sends Aaron to meet Moses
Speaks to the people for Moses
les: Aaron helped hold up Moses' tired arms. Whose hands could you strengthen this week?
Aaron failed badly with the calf, yet God kept using him. How does God's patience with Aaron encourage you?

name: Joshua
bio: Joshua served as Moses' minister and was one of only two spies who trusted God to give Israel the land. After Moses died, God called him to lead Israel across the Jordan. He led the conquest of Canaan, beginning with the fall of Jericho, and divided the land among the tribes. At the end of his life he challenged Israel to choose whom they would serve.
tl: Brings a good report of the land
Be strong and of a good courage
As for me and my house
les: God told Joshua three times to be strong and courageous. What fear do you need to hand over to God's promise of His presence?
'As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.' What would that choice look like in your home today?

name: Rahab
bio: Rahab was a harlot in Jericho who hid the two Israelite spies and confessed faith in the LORD as God of heaven and earth. She asked for mercy for her family and was told to bind a scarlet thread in her window. When Jericho fell, she and her household were saved. She became an ancestor of David and of Jesus, and is honored for her faith in Hebrews.
les: Rahab's past did not stop God from saving her. How does her story speak to the shame anyone might carry?
She acted on faith before she saw Jericho fall. What does living faith look like for you this week?

name: Deborah
bio: Deborah was a prophetess and judge in Israel who held court under a palm tree. She summoned Barak to lead Israel against Sisera, the captain of Jabin's army. When Barak would not go without her, she went with him, and God gave Israel the victory. Her song in Judges 5 praises God for delivering His people.
tl: Judges Israel under the palm tree
Up; for this is the day
The land has rest forty years
les: Deborah encouraged Barak with God's promise. Who might God want you to encourage with His Word?
She gave all the glory to God in song. How can you praise God publicly for His help?

name: Gideon
meaning: he that bruises or breaks; a destroyer
bio: Gideon was threshing wheat in hiding when the angel of the LORD called him a mighty man of valour. Unsure of himself, he asked God for signs with a fleece. God reduced his army to three hundred men so Israel would know the victory was the LORD's. With trumpets, pitchers and lamps they routed the Midianites.
les: God saw a mighty man where Gideon saw weakness. How might God see you differently than you see yourself?
God made Gideon's army small so no one could boast. Where is God working through your weakness?

name: Samson
meaning: his sun; his service; there the second time
bio: Samson was a Nazarite from birth whom God gave great strength to begin delivering Israel from the Philistines. He did mighty deeds, yet he was ruled by his desires and trifled with his vow. Delilah learned the secret of his strength, and he was captured, blinded and imprisoned. In his death he called on God once more and brought down the temple of Dagon.
tl: Slays a thousand with a jawbone
les: Samson's gifts were great, but his choices led him into bondage. What boundaries help protect your walk with God?
Even at the end, Samson prayed and God answered. How does that show God's mercy toward those who return to Him?

name: Ruth
bio: Ruth was a Moabite woman who married into an Israelite family living in Moab. After her husband died, she refused to leave her mother-in-law Naomi and pledged herself to Naomi's people and God. Gleaning in the fields of Boaz, she found kindness, and Boaz redeemed her as kinsman and married her. She became the great-grandmother of King David and is named in the genealogy of Jesus.
tl: Whither thou goest, I will go
Gleans in the field of Boaz
Mother of Obed, grandfather of David
les: Ruth chose loyal love when leaving would have been easier. Who has God placed in your life to love faithfully?
Boaz the kinsman-redeemer points to Jesus, who redeems us. How does Ruth's story help you rest under the wings of God?

name: Naomi
bio: Naomi moved with her husband and sons from Bethlehem to Moab during a famine. There her husband and both sons died, and she returned home bitter, asking to be called Mara. Through her daughter-in-law Ruth and the kindness of Boaz, God restored her hope. She held the newborn Obed, and the women praised God for giving her a redeemer.
tl: Goes to Moab in a famine
les: Naomi was honest with God about her grief. How can you bring your sorrow to Him without pretending?
God was working for Naomi's good even when she felt empty. Where might He be quietly at work in your life now?

name: Hannah
bio: Hannah was a wife of Elkanah who grieved for years because she had no children. At Shiloh she poured out her soul before the LORD and vowed to give her son back to Him. God remembered her and she bore Samuel, whom she brought to serve at the house of the LORD. Her prayer of praise rejoices in a God who lifts up the humble.
tl: Vows her son to the LORD
les: Hannah poured out her heart honestly to God. What burden could you pour out before Him today?
She gave back to God the gift she had longed for. What has God given you that you can offer back to Him?

name: Samuel
meaning: heard of God; asked of God
bio: Samuel was the answer to Hannah's prayer and grew up serving the LORD under Eli at Shiloh. As a boy he heard God call him by name. He became a prophet, judge and priest who led Israel in repentance. He anointed Israel's first two kings, Saul and David.
tl: Ministers before the LORD as a child
Hitherto hath the LORD helped us
To obey is better than sacrifice
les: 'Speak; for thy servant heareth.' How can you make space to listen for God through His Word?
Samuel learned that God looks on the heart. How does that change how you see others, and yourself?

name: Saul
bio: Saul, a tall Benjamite, was anointed by Samuel as Israel's first king. He began humbly and won victories, but he grew impatient and disobedient to God's commands. God rejected him as king and chose David, whom Saul came to envy and pursue. He died in battle with the Philistines on mount Gilboa.
tl: Spares Agag and the best spoil
les: Saul's partial obedience was still disobedience. Is there an area where God is asking for full obedience from you?
Envy consumed Saul. How can you celebrate others' blessings instead of competing with them?

name: David
bio: David was the youngest son of Jesse, a shepherd anointed by Samuel to be king. He defeated Goliath trusting in the LORD, then endured years of being hunted by Saul. As king he united Israel, brought the ark to Jerusalem and received God's promise of an everlasting throne. Though he sinned grievously with Bathsheba, he repented deeply, and many of his psalms express faith and worship.
les: David ran toward Goliath because he trusted God's name. What giant are you facing that needs that kind of faith?
After his sin, David prayed, 'Create in me a clean heart.' How can his honest repentance guide you back to God?

name: Solomon
bio: Solomon was the son of David and Bathsheba who became king after his father. When God offered him anything, he asked for an understanding heart, and God gave him wisdom, riches and honor. He built the temple in Jerusalem and wrote many proverbs. In later life his many foreign wives turned his heart toward other gods.
tl: Asks God for an understanding heart
les: Solomon asked for wisdom rather than riches. What would you ask God for if you could ask for anything?
Even the wisest king drifted when his heart divided. What helps keep your heart wholly devoted to God?

name: Elijah
meaning: God the Lord, the strong Lord
bio: Elijah was a prophet from Gilead who confronted King Ahab and the worship of Baal. God fed him by ravens and provided for the widow of Zarephath through him. On mount Carmel he called down fire from heaven, and the people declared, 'The LORD, he is the God.' After fleeing in discouragement, he heard God's still small voice, and he was finally taken up to heaven in a whirlwind.
tl: Asks to die under a juniper tree
les: After a great victory Elijah felt alone and exhausted, and God cared for his body first. How can you let God meet you in weariness?
God spoke in a still small voice, not the earthquake. How are you making room to hear Him quietly?

name: Elisha
bio: Elisha was plowing when Elijah cast his mantle on him, and he left everything to follow. He asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit and saw him taken up to heaven. His ministry was full of miracles of mercy: healing waters, multiplying oil, raising a child, and healing Naaman. He showed his servant the hosts of God surrounding them.
tl: They that be with us are more
Eyes opened to chariots of fire
les: Elisha left his oxen to follow God's call. What might you need to leave behind to follow Him more fully?
'They that be with us are more than they that be with them.' Where do you need to see God's unseen help?

name: Esther
bio: Esther was a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, who became queen of Persia. When Haman plotted to destroy the Jews, Mordecai urged her to speak to the king. She called for fasting and went before the king uninvited, saying, 'If I perish, I perish.' God used her courage to save her people, remembered each year at Purim.
tl: For such a time as this
The king holds out the sceptre
les: Esther was placed where she was 'for such a time as this.' Where has God placed you to make a difference?
She prepared with fasting before she acted. How can prayer come first before your hard conversations?

name: Daniel
meaning: judgment of God; God my judge
bio: Daniel was taken captive to Babylon as a young man and purposed in his heart not to defile himself. God gave him wisdom to interpret Nebuchadnezzar's dreams and the writing on the wall. He kept praying three times a day even when it was forbidden, and God shut the lions' mouths. He served faithfully under several kings and received visions of God's coming kingdom.
tl: Reads the writing on the wall
Vision of the Son of man
les: Daniel decided ahead of time to stay faithful. What convictions do you want to settle in your heart before pressure comes?
He kept his prayer habit even under threat. How can steady prayer anchor you in uncertain times?

name: Jonah
meaning: or Jonas, a dove; he that oppresses; destroyer
bio: Jonah was a prophet God sent to call the great city of Nineveh to repentance. He fled the other way by ship, was thrown into the sea, and was swallowed by a great fish. From inside the fish he prayed, and God brought him to dry land. Nineveh repented, but Jonah was angry at God's mercy, and God gently taught him about His compassion.
les: Jonah ran from God's call but could not outrun God's love. Is there something you have been avoiding that God is calling you to?
Jonah wanted mercy for himself but not for Nineveh. Who might God want you to see with His compassion?

name: Isaiah
bio: Isaiah was a prophet in Jerusalem during the reigns of several kings of Judah. In a vision he saw the Lord high and lifted up and answered, 'Here am I; send me.' He warned of judgment and called Judah to trust God rather than foreign powers. His prophecies of the virgin's son, the Prince of Peace and the suffering Servant are fulfilled in Jesus.
tl: Sees the Lord high and lifted up
Unto us a child is born
He was wounded for our transgressions
les: Seeing God's holiness made Isaiah aware of his own need, and then of God's cleansing. How does worship change how you see yourself?
Isaiah saw Jesus' suffering centuries ahead. How does Isaiah 53 deepen your gratitude for the cross?

name: Jeremiah
bio: Jeremiah was called as a young man to be a prophet to the nations. For about forty years he warned Judah of coming judgment, often rejected, mocked and imprisoned. He wept over his people and saw Jerusalem fall to Babylon. He also spoke of hope, a future and a new covenant written on the heart.
tl: A fire shut up in my bones
les: God knew Jeremiah before he was born. How does being known by God shape your sense of purpose?
Jeremiah kept speaking truth when it cost him. Where might God be asking you to stay faithful when it is hard?

name: Job
bio: Job was a man of Uz who was perfect and upright, fearing God and turning away from evil. Satan claimed Job served God only for blessings, and God permitted Job to be tested with the loss of his children, wealth and health. Job grieved and questioned, yet did not curse God. When God spoke out of the whirlwind, Job humbled himself, and the LORD restored him and blessed his latter end.
tl: The LORD gave, the LORD hath taken
I know that my redeemer liveth
God answers out of the whirlwind
les: Job brought his questions to God rather than walking away. How can you be honest with God in suffering?
Job did not get every answer, but he met God. How does knowing God matter more than knowing why?

name: Mary (mother of Jesus)
bio: Mary was a young virgin of Nazareth, engaged to Joseph, when the angel Gabriel told her she would bear the Son of God. She humbly answered, 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord.' She gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem and pondered all that happened in her heart. She stood by the cross and was with the disciples in prayer after His resurrection.
tl: Behold the handmaid of the Lord
My soul doth magnify the Lord
Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it
les: Mary said yes to God without knowing everything ahead. What would it look like to say, 'Be it unto me according to thy word'?
She treasured and pondered what God was doing. How can you make time to reflect on God's work in your life?

name: John the Baptist
meaning: the grace or mercy of the Lord
bio: John was the son of the priest Zacharias and Elisabeth, born in their old age. He lived in the wilderness and preached repentance, preparing the way for the Lord. He baptized Jesus in the Jordan and pointed others to Him as the Lamb of God. He was imprisoned by Herod for speaking the truth and was beheaded.
les: 'He must increase, but I must decrease.' Where can you point attention away from yourself and toward Jesus?
John's message was repentance. Is there anything God is lovingly calling you to turn from?

name: Peter
bio: Simon Peter was a fisherman whom Jesus called to become a fisher of men. Bold and impulsive, he confessed Jesus as the Christ, walked on water, and later denied Him three times. After the resurrection Jesus restored him with the question, 'Lovest thou me?' Filled with the Holy Ghost, Peter preached at Pentecost and became a leader of the early church.
tl: Called to be a fisher of men
Freed from prison by an angel
les: Jesus restored Peter after his worst failure. What failure do you need to let Jesus restore?
Peter began to sink when he looked at the waves. Where do you need to keep your eyes on Jesus?

name: John (the apostle)
meaning: the grace or mercy of the Lord
bio: John, the son of Zebedee, was a fisherman called by Jesus with his brother James. He was one of the three closest to Jesus and is traditionally identified as 'the disciple whom Jesus loved.' At the cross Jesus entrusted His mother to him. He wrote the Gospel of John, three letters, and the Revelation, with a deep emphasis on love.
les: John knew himself as one loved by Jesus. How would your day change if you lived from that identity?
'We love him, because he first loved us.' How can you show God's love to someone this week?

name: Mary Magdalene
bio: Mary Magdalene was a woman from whom Jesus cast out seven devils. She followed Him and helped support His ministry. She stood near the cross and came early to the tomb on the first day of the week. The risen Jesus appeared first to her, calling her by name, and sent her to tell the disciples.
les: Jesus called Mary by name in her grief. How does it comfort you that He knows your name?
She was the first to announce the resurrection. Who could you share the good news with?

name: Martha and Mary
bio: Martha and Mary were sisters in Bethany, with their brother Lazarus, and close friends of Jesus. Martha was busy serving while Mary sat at Jesus' feet, and Jesus gently said Mary had chosen the good part. When Lazarus died, Martha confessed Jesus as the Christ, and Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead. Mary later anointed Jesus with costly ointment.
les: Jesus valued Martha's service but invited her to rest at His feet. Where can you trade anxious busyness for time with Him?
In grief Martha said, 'I believe.' How can you hold onto faith even when your questions remain?

name: Paul
bio: Paul, first called Saul, was a zealous Pharisee who persecuted the church. The risen Jesus met him on the road to Damascus, and he became an apostle to the Gentiles. He travelled widely, planting churches and writing letters that form much of the New Testament. He suffered greatly for Christ and finished his course faithfully.
tl: Light from heaven on the Damascus road
les: God transformed Paul from persecutor to apostle. Is there anyone you think is beyond God's reach?
Paul sang in prison. How can you worship God even when circumstances are hard?

name: Timothy
meaning: honor of God; valued of God
bio: Timothy was a young believer from Lystra, raised in faith by his mother Eunice and grandmother Lois. Paul took him as a travelling companion and called him his own son in the faith. He served as Paul's trusted helper and led the church at Ephesus. Paul's two letters to him encourage him to be bold and faithful.
tl: Let no man despise thy youth
Stir up the gift of God
les: Timothy's faith began at home. Who passed faith on to you, and who could you pass it on to?
'God hath not given us the spirit of fear.' Where do you need God's power, love and sound mind today?

name: Priscilla
bio: Priscilla and her husband Aquila were Jewish tentmakers who worked alongside Paul in Corinth. They travelled with him to Ephesus and hosted a church in their home. Together they took Apollos aside and explained the way of God more perfectly. Paul honored them as helpers who risked their lives for him.
les: Priscilla and Aquila served God together through their work and home. How can your home be a place of welcome?
They gently taught Apollos in private. How can you encourage others in truth with grace?

name: Abigail
bio: Abigail was the wise and beautiful wife of Nabal, a harsh and foolish man. When Nabal insulted David, she quickly brought provisions and humbly persuaded David not to take revenge. David blessed God for her good counsel. After Nabal died, David took Abigail as his wife.
les: Abigail's quick, humble wisdom stopped a disaster. How can you be a peacemaker in a tense situation?
She reminded David of God's purposes for him. Who can you encourage with God's truth this week?
